candidates.basis: NL9 contract; source trace trace:state:Approaching; closed state state:Approaching:line:24; closed action inventory represented by lifecycle projection Approaching:5:Decelerate; no supplied exact action for continued approach.
candidates.expected: Approaching performs an ongoing action that continues to approach the destination.
candidates.observed: Approaching has only the closed lifecycle entry action Decelerate; no supplied action represents continuing to approach the destination.

The exact primary explicit-member reading has required count 3 and observed count 0. A direct-child interpretation is a weaker alternative and is not needed to establish the explicit named-member violation; the sentence itself names the required members.
decisions.violated_obligation: The InMotion scope realizes the three named substates Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching.

decisions.basis: NL2, exact Stopping binding, source reachability certificate, V4 inputs, and completed native progress check.
decisions.reason: The contract requires the reachable non-final Stopping operating state to retain continuation. Exact facts show Stopping is reachable, non-final, and has no outgoing or inherited transitions; the V4 native check also found no committed successor. No supplied final edge, terminal clause, concurrent region, or inherited continuation supports an intentional-terminal reading.
decisions.violated_obligation: The reachable non-final Stopping state admits continuation rather than ending at a dead leaf.

decisions.basis: NL2 alternative, exact InMotion-to-Stopping transition binding, and supplied guard fact.
decisions.reason: The alternative contract requires the InMotion-to-Stopping transition to retain the independent guard "the system arrives". The exact carrier transition has guard null. The transition's event or trigger field is distinct from the guard field and cannot satisfy this obligation.
decisions.violated_obligation: The InMotion-to-Stopping transition has the required guard "the system arrives".

decisions.basis: NL5 alternative, exact Accelerating-to-Cruising transition binding, and supplied guard fact.
decisions.reason: The contract requires the Accelerating-to-Cruising transition to have the independent guard "cruising speed is reached". The exact carrier has guard null. No supplied fact equates another transition field with this guard.
decisions.violated_obligation: The Accelerating-to-Cruising transition has the required cruising-speed guard.

decisions.basis: NL6 alternative, exact Accelerating-to-Approaching transition binding, and supplied guard fact.
decisions.reason: The contract requires the Accelerating-to-Approaching transition to have the independent guard "approaches its destination". The exact carrier has guard null. Its event or trigger field is a different typed property and does not rebut the missing guard.
decisions.violated_obligation: The Accelerating-to-Approaching transition has the required destination-approach guard.

decisions.basis: NL7 alternative, exact Cruising-to-Approaching transition binding, and supplied guard fact.
decisions.reason: The contract requires the Cruising-to-Approaching transition to have the independent guard "approaches the destination". The exact carrier has guard null. No supplied fact makes its event or trigger field a substitute for the required guard.
decisions.violated_obligation: The Cruising-to-Approaching transition has the required destination-approach guard.

decisions.basis: NL1 derived scenario, exact event and target bindings, and completed native runtime trace.
decisions.reason: The contract requires the exact Closed/SendDeparted stimulus to enter InMotion. The native runtime trace consumes that stimulus and shows InMotion active at the post-stimulus step, followed by Accelerating in the trailing observation. Thus the supplied exact runtime facts do not establish the alleged wrong-target reading.
decisions.violated_obligation: After Closed/SendDeparted, the artifact enters InMotion.

decisions.basis: NL4 containment clause, exact Accelerating and InMotion bindings, and closed-model parent facts.
decisions.reason: The quoted contract requires Accelerating within InMotion. Exact model facts place Accelerating at the root and mark InMotion non-composite. The existence of an InMotion-to-Accelerating transition describes an endpoint relation, not hierarchical containment.
decisions.violated_obligation: Accelerating is contained within InMotion.

decisions.basis: NL5 derived scenario, exact event and target bindings, and the dossier's native-runtime alternative.
decisions.reason: The contract requires Reached Cruising/Cruise to move the system to Cruising, but this dossier supplies only exact event and target bindings and explicitly delegates post-stimulus state evaluation to a runtime scenario. No runtime result or exact state trace is supplied here, so the alleged wrong-target reading cannot be decided.
decisions.violated_obligation: After Reached Cruising/Cruise, the artifact enters Cruising.

decisions.basis: NL6 derived scenario, exact event and target bindings, and the dossier's native-runtime alternative.
decisions.reason: The contract requires Approached/Decelerate to move the system to Approaching, but the dossier supplies no resulting runtime trace or equivalent exact state fact. Exact binding alone does not decide whether the required target becomes active.
decisions.violated_obligation: After Approached/Decelerate, the artifact enters Approaching.

decisions.basis: NL4 containment clause, exact Cruising and InMotion bindings, and closed-model parent facts.
decisions.reason: The quoted contract requires Cruising within InMotion. Exact model facts place Cruising at the root and identify InMotion as non-composite. The supplied InMotion-to-Cruising and Cruising-to-Approaching transitions do not establish containment.
decisions.violated_obligation: Cruising is contained within InMotion.

decisions.basis: NL4 containment clause, exact Approaching and InMotion bindings, and closed-model parent facts.
decisions.reason: The quoted contract requires Approaching within InMotion. Exact model facts place Approaching at the root and identify InMotion as non-composite. The InMotion-to-Approaching transition is only an endpoint relation and does not rebut the containment defect.
decisions.violated_obligation: Approaching is contained within InMotion.

decisions.basis: NL5 initial-entry clause, exact InMotion and Accelerating bindings, and supplied source/model entry facts.
decisions.reason: The contract requires InMotion's default entry to target Accelerating. Exact facts show no InMotion-owned initial pseudostate or composite default entry; transition:line:32 is a normal transition. Reaching Accelerating through that normal edge does not provide initial-entry semantics.
decisions.violated_obligation: InMotion has an owner-local initial entry targeting Accelerating.

decisions.basis: NL9 effect clause, exact Approaching binding, and closed lifecycle/effect inventory.
decisions.reason: The contract requires Approaching to send the "Send" signal. Exact lifecycle facts show only entry action Decelerate and no Send effect. The presence of event declarations or incoming triggers does not establish an effect emitted by Approaching.
decisions.violated_obligation: Approaching sends the Send signal.

decisions.basis: NL9 ongoing-action clause, exact Approaching binding, and supplied lifecycle/action inventory.
decisions.reason: The contract requires an ongoing action that continues approaching the destination. Exact facts show only entry action Decelerate; the structural outgoing transitions do not constitute the separately required ongoing action. The issue is absence of the specified action, not absence of all transitions.
decisions.violated_obligation: Approaching performs an ongoing action that continues approach to the destination.

decisions.basis: NL9 ongoing-action clause, exact Approaching binding, and supplied trace and lifecycle facts.
decisions.reason: The contract says that in Approaching the system continues to approach the destination. The exact state is bound, and the supplied action inventory contains only entry action Decelerate, with no action representing continued approach. Outgoing transitions to Stopping or final do not establish that action property.
decisions.violated_obligation: Approaching represents the required continuing approach behavior.

decisions.basis: NL10 retention clause, exact Approaching binding, and the supplied absence of retention scenario facts.
decisions.reason: The contract requires remaining in Approaching while nearing the destination until the specified stopping or deceleration condition. The exact state is bound, but the dossier supplies no conditional stimulus, state window, trace, or retention fact. Outgoing exits show possible transitions but neither prove nor disprove retention under the stated condition.
decisions.violated_obligation: The system remains in Approaching under the specified nearing-destination condition until it is ready to stop or decelerate.

result.reason: All 20 required obligation IDs are represented exactly once. The supplied exact facts establish violations for the missing effects, containment, initial-entry, guard, cardinality, action, and dead-end obligations; they do not establish the trigger or successful Closed/SendDeparted transition violations; and the two runtime scenarios plus the conditional retention requirement remain undecided where their required outcome facts are absent.

issues.basis: NL1; source transition tr_0002; closed transition:line:28 and event:Closed_SendDeparted:line:2.
issues.reason: The exact DoorsClosing-to-InMotion transition carries Closed_SendDeparted, which corresponds to the required source signal, so no semantic mismatch is established.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The normalized closed event is the exact authored signal; the apparent spelling difference is representation normalization, not a mismatch.

issues.basis: NL3; exact source state EmergencyStopping; FCSTM state:EmergencyStopping:line:15; no effect appears in the closed lifecycle/effect inventory.
issues.observed: EmergencyStopping declares only entry action EmergencyStop; no Obstacle Detected effect is present.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The Obstacle Detected event is present as the incoming InMotion trigger, but no supplied fact makes that incoming trigger an effect emitted by EmergencyStopping.
issues.title: EmergencyStopping Missing Obstacle Detected Effect

issues.reason: The source requires Accelerating within InMotion, while the closed model places both as root-level states and marks InMotion non-composite.

issues.basis: NL4; exact source inventory parents are null; inspection-equivalent state inventory shows InMotion is non-composite and Cruising parent is the root.
issues.observed: Cruising is a root-level state and InMotion is non-composite in the closed model.
issues.reason: The source requires Cruising within InMotion, while the closed model places both as root-level states and marks InMotion non-composite.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The closed model has InMotion-to-Cruising and Cruising-to-Approaching transitions, but those edges do not establish hierarchical containment.
issues.title: Cruising Is Not Contained In InMotion

issues.basis: NL4; exact source inventory parents are null; inspection-equivalent state inventory shows InMotion is non-composite and Approaching parent is the root.
issues.observed: Approaching is a root-level state and InMotion is non-composite in the closed model.
issues.reason: The source requires Approaching within InMotion, while the closed model places both as root-level states and marks InMotion non-composite.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The model's InMotion-to-Approaching transition is an endpoint relation only and does not prove containment.
issues.title: Approaching Is Not Contained In InMotion

issues.basis: NL5; FCSTM inspection inventory shows InMotion is non-composite; transition:line:32 has source InMotion and no pseudostate source.
issues.expected: InMotion's owner-local initial entry targets Accelerating.
issues.observed: No InMotion-owned initial edge exists; transition:line:32 is a normal InMotion-to-Accelerating edge.
issues.reason: The source requires InMotion to initially enter Accelerating. The closed model has no InMotion-owned initial pseudostate or composite default entry; the unguarded InMotion-to-Accelerating edge is a normal transition, not an initial edge.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The normal InMotion-to-Accelerating edge reaches the named state, but it does not establish default entry semantics.
issues.title: InMotion Lacks Required Initial Entry

issues.basis: NL9; exact state mapping; FCSTM state declaration and effect inventory contain no Send effect.
issues.observed: Approaching declares entry action Decelerate and no Send effect.
issues.reason: The source independently requires Approaching to send Send. The closed Approaching state has only an entry Decelerate action and no Send effect.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The closed model declares a Send-like source event only in the author NL, while the FCSTM contains no corresponding effect declaration.
issues.title: Approaching Missing Send Effect

issues.basis: NL9; exact Approaching state binding; FCSTM state declaration lists only entry Decelerate and no ongoing approach action.
issues.expected: Approaching performs an ongoing action that continues approach to the destination.
issues.observed: Approaching has only entry action Decelerate; no continuing-approach action is declared.
issues.reason: The source explicitly requires continued approach while in Approaching. The closed model has structural exits but no exact ongoing action representing that behavior.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The outgoing Ready_to_Stop and Destination_Missed transitions provide structural continuation, but neither is the required ongoing action.
issues.title: Approaching Lacks Continuing Approach Action

issues.basis: NL9 contract; source trace trace:state:Approaching; closed state state:Approaching:line:24; closed action inventory represented by lifecycle projection Approaching:5:Decelerate; no supplied exact action for continued approach.
issues.expected: Approaching performs an ongoing action that continues to approach the destination.
issues.observed: Approaching has only the closed lifecycle entry action Decelerate; no supplied action represents continuing to approach the destination.
issues.reason: The exact Approaching state is root-reachable and has outgoing transitions to Stopping and final, but its supplied lifecycle/action inventory contains only the entry action Decelerate. The required ongoing behavior to continue approaching is therefore not represented by the closed state action carrier. This is an action-property issue, not a deadlock claim.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The outgoing Ready_to_Stop and Destination_Missed transitions could provide operational progress, but they do not establish the separately required ongoing action of continuing to approach the destination.
issues.title: Approaching lacks required continuation behavior

issues.basis: NL10 contract; exact Approaching source/model binding; supplied verify facts contain reachability and deadlock checks only, while SMT formulas are empty and no trace facts are supplied.
issues.expected: The system remains in Approaching while nearing the destination until it is ready to stop or decelerate.
issues.observed: No supplied trace or executable retention fact evaluates this conditional state-retention requirement.
issues.reason: The exact Approaching state is bound, but the closure supplies no scenario, stimulus, state-window, trace, or native retention fact for evaluating the stated conditional retention behavior. The precise obligation is preserved as a semantic candidate rather than replaced with an endpoint or reachability claim.
issues.requirement_quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The presence of outgoing Ready_to_Stop and Destination_Missed transitions shows possible exits, but does not prove or disprove retention under the specified nearing-destination condition.
issues.title: Approaching retention is not expressible by supplied evidence

issues.basis: NL4 exact named-member cardinality binding; source inventory identifies InMotion, Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching as root-level states; closed inspection inventory marks InMotion non-composite and gives all three required states parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034.
issues.expected: InMotion owns exactly the three explicitly named operating substates Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching.
issues.observed: The closed model has InMotion as a non-composite state; the three named states are root-level siblings, so the required InMotion-owned member domain is not realized.
issues.reason: The source contract requires exactly three explicitly named operating substates under InMotion. The closed model binds InMotion as a non-composite state, while Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching are all root-level siblings rather than contained descendants. The typed cardinality binding is exact; this candidate preserves the resulting structural mismatch without converting it into an endpoint or reachability issue.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The closed model contains all three named states and transitions among them, but those facts do not establish the required containment under InMotion.
issues.title: InMotion has no explicit operating-substate structure

issues.basis: NL5 owner/target contract; source inventory identifies InMotion and Accelerating as root-level source states; closed inspection inventory marks InMotion non-composite and supplies only transition:line:27 as the root initial edge to DoorsClosing.
issues.expected: Entering the InMotion scope initially enters Accelerating through an InMotion-owned initial edge.
issues.observed: No InMotion-owned initial edge exists; InMotion is a non-composite closed state and the only initial edge is root -> DoorsClosing.
issues.reason: Accelerating is an exact required target, but the closed model has no composite InMotion owner-local initial edge. The only initial edge is the root edge to DoorsClosing, and InMotion is parsed as a leaf. A root initial edge cannot satisfy the distinct nested InMotion-to-Accelerating entry obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The closed model has an InMotion-to-Accelerating transition at transition:line:32, but it is a normal transition and does not constitute an owner-local initial pseudostate edge.
issues.title: InMotion lacks the required owner-local initial entry
